chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) ordered an old man who had never performed Hajj and was unable to perform it due to his old age to equip a man to perform Hajj on his behalf.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an elderly person who cannot physically perform Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *Hajj al-Tamattu'* (or *Hajj al-Ni'ab*) for the living elderly who lack the physical capacity to perform the pilgrimage themselves. It highlights the scholarly consensus that the proxy must be fully equipped and sent by the incapable person, ensuring the obligation is fulfilled through a valid representative rather than a voluntary substitute. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of religious duties (*Fara'id*) even when personal performance becomes impossible due to age or infirmity.
